paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the vocabulary size of four languages—Spanish, Korean, Korean, and Japanese—as a function of the number of iterations. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Iterations,” displays a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 500, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 50. The y-axis, labeled “Vocabulary of Size,” ranges from 0 to approximately 5000, also on a linear scale with tick labels spaced at intervals of 200. A solid blue line represents the average vocabulary size across all four languages and ten different starting words, while four shaded lines in orange, green, and teal represent the individual vocabulary size curves for each of the four languages, each derived from a different starting word. At the beginning of the x-axis (iteration 0), all lines intersect at a vocabulary size of approximately 300, and at the end of the x-axis (iteration 500), the Spanish line reaches a vocabulary size of approximately 4800, the Korean line reaches a vocabulary size of approximately 4700, the Korean line reaches a vocabulary size of approximately 4600, and the Japanese line reaches a vocabulary size of approximately 3800.
